title: The $5M Heist Where 64 Minutes Vanished — Then the Bodies Started Piling Up
description:
On December 11th, 1978, six masked men robbed the Lufthansa cargo terminal at JFK in just 64 minutes — no alarms, no shots fired, and no one caught in the act. It became the largest cash robbery in American history at the time, made possible by an inside tip from a debt-ridden cargo worker and orchestrated by Lucchese associate Jimmy Burke.

The getaway van should have destroyed the evidence. It didn't. A single surviving fingerprint sent one man to prison — but he wasn't the mastermind. Within a year, at least eight people connected to the heist turned up dead, killed in freezer trucks, meat trucks, and car trunks, as Burke allegedly erased his own crew to keep the money for himself.

Burke was never charged for the robbery. Of the $5.875 million stolen, only about $20,000 was ever recovered. Decades later, the rest of the money — and the true body count — remains a mystery.
